Beállítom Dunaszentbenedeknél a Duna medrében épül a fenékküszöb, ennek részeként összesen 117, egyenként 2,5 tonnás betonkockákat dobál helikopterről a Dunába a Magyar Honvédség, jelentette be vasárnapi videójában Ruszin-Szendi Romulusz. A honvédelmi miniszter azt mondta, a vízügyesek közlése szerint 13 méter volt a vízmélység vasárnap reggel. A szakértők szerint óriási szükség van ezekre a kövekre, mert „amit nappal építünk, az este leomlik, mint ahogy a balladában is van”, mondta Ruszin-Szendi, utalva a Kőmíves Kelemen népballadára. „Felmegyünk majd a fedélzetre és megnézzük felülről, hogy jó helyre viszi-e az ár a követ a nap végén. Bízunk benne, hogy tényleg sikerül megfogni a meder alját.” Magyar Péter szombaton jelentette be , hogy még aznap, két héttel a határidő előtt elkészül az első ütem Paksnál, összeér a fenékküszöb a Duna teljes szélességében. A miniszterelnök „elképesztő emberi és szakmai teljesítménynek” nevezte mindezt. Kifejtette véleményét fenékküszöb-ügyben nemrég Bardóczi Sándor fővárosi főtájépítész is. Szerinte nem a kapkodás és a kivitelezési hibák jelentik a problémát, hanem az, ha ez a sebtében megépített fenékküszöb így marad. „Az a környezetvédelmi, természetvédelmi, vízügyi hatóságok nem egyszerű feladata lesz, hogy merjék kimondani, ami a katasztrófa elkerülése miatt sebtében a Dunában megépült, az így nem maradhat meg, s kell egy ettől eltérő alternatív megoldást kiépíteni, ami nem csak az energiabiztonságot szolgálja, hanem az összes többi szempontot is.” Az elmúlt hetek forrósága, illetve a kialakult rekordalacsony vízállás miatt a hónap elején majdnem teljesen le kellett állítani a paksi atomerőművet, mert a működéséhez szükséges hűtővizet a rendszer már alig-alig tudta kivenni a Dunából. Teljes leállás végül nem volt, egy turbinát működésben tudtak tartani. A kellő mennyiségű víz biztosítása érdekében a kormány augusztus 12-én bárkák alkalmazásáról és egy fenékküszöb építéséről döntött. A munkálatokhoz Magyar Péter szerint „kisebb noszogatásra”, de egészen távoli bányákból is ajánlottak fel követ, mások mellett Orbán Győző, Orbán Viktor apja is . A most részben elkészült dunai fenékküszöb gyors megoldást jelent az atomerőmű működésének biztosítására, ami azóta egyébként újra teljes kapacitással üzemel. Múlt szombaton kezdték el visszakapcsolni a harmadik turbinát, hétfőn négyből három blokk már teljes kapacitáson működött . A miniszterelnök szerint abban, hogy a paksi erőmű újra csúcson termel nagy szerepe van a fenékküszöbnek is. https://bnn-news.com/protest-at-kaunas-m.text: Photo: Noah Holm/Unsplash Advertisement Kaunas police announced the launch of a pre-trial investigation regarding the alleged incitement of hatred based on nationality, race, ethnicity, religion, or other grounds, as well as the disruption of religious rituals. Authorities have also initiated administrative proceedings because the organizers had not obtained a permit for the gathering. Several motorcycle clubs were involved in the protest at the mosque, including Roadhogs MC, Vilkai MC, and Vorai MC. Representatives of the clubs were reluctant to discuss the event; however, one individual who wished to remain anonymous stated that the bikers were protesting against disorder surrounding the mosque. He told LRT that traffic and public order are disrupted when prayers take place in the mosque's courtyard. The main issue, he claimed, was the total lack of order and a lack of respect for Lithuanian citizens and others in the vicinity. The protest was reportedly not directed against Islam itself, but rather intended to demonstrate that holding prayers in a public space and disturbing local residents is unacceptable. Nevertheless, the protest is widely regarded as a hostile act against Muslims. Legal expert Skirmantas Bikelis stated that Lithuanian politicians missed an opportunity to respond quickly and condemn what he described as a hate crime. Arūnas Kučikas, Director of Caritas for the Archdiocese of Kaunas and Chairman of the Caritas Lithuania Council, pointed out that attempts to intimidate a religious community during prayer—particularly through the use of historically significant symbols—can have serious consequences. Kučikas noted that Christians do not advocate merely for abstract tolerance; while one may disagree with religious content, a community should not be denied the opportunity to pray, nor should its members be intimidated or frightened. He added that the use of a pig's head in the protest evoked historical episodes of persecution, including pogroms and attacks against Jews. Advertisement Lithuanian courts have previously dealt with incidents involving pig carcass parts used to attack Jews. In 2013, a court in Šilutė convicted a man after he nailed two pig ears to the doors of the former Švėkšna synagogue. The court concluded that the man's actions constituted public mockery and the incitement of hatred against Jews. In 2015, a court in Kaunas sentenced Jevgenijus Pleganovas, who in 2010 had placed a pig's head—wearing a hat and with sidelocks glued to it—outside the Kaunas synagogue. The consumption of pork is forbidden in both Islam and Judaism; consequently, the animal is considered offensive in both religions. Egdūnas Račius, a professor of Islamic and Muslim community studies at Vytautas Magnus University, noted that Advertisement in Western societies, the pig is known as a symbol used to deliberately offend Muslims. However, he cautioned that the symbolism of the pig is not so easily explained from a Muslim perspective. While presenting a pig's head is a classic example of "everyday Orientalism," some Muslims—particularly those from regions where pigs are rarely encountered—might not immediately grasp the intent behind the gesture. Meanwhile, Milda Ališauskienė, a professor of sociology and religious studies at Vytautas Magnus University, stated that the incident in Kaunas reflects a shift in how such acts are carried out. While pig heads used to be placed secretly in the past, people can now be seen standing proudly while holding a pig's head, seeking to humiliate members of other races and religions. This raises questions about whether Lithuanian society has become more tolerant of hatred based on religion and race. Kučikas said the incident highlights the need for stronger dialogue among religious communities, alongside greater involvement from Kaunas municipal authorities. He acknowledged that tensions have escalated in recent years between Kaunas’s historic Tatar Muslim community and a newer community formed more recently, but noted that these issues could be resolved through dialogue rather than confrontation. Kučikas emphasized the lack of established interfaith communication practices in Kaunas—and Lithuania as a whole—and called on religious leaders to meet regularly to discuss shared issues, including the right of each group to practice its own religion. The Archdiocese of Kaunas also condemned the protest, stating its opposition to the disruption of prayers and the display of disrespect toward Islam. Archbishop Kęstutis Kėvalas emphasized that religious freedom and the preservation of human dignity are integral parts of a mature, democratic society. One may disagree, hold different worldviews, or offer criticism, but one must not humiliate a person because of their religious beliefs. Bikelis pointed out that previous court rulings demonstrate that displaying or placing a pig's head near religious buildings can be considered an act of humiliation, mockery, and incitement of hatred. However, he noted that a recent appellate court ruling regarding statements made by former MP Petras Gražulis complicates the legal assessment. Gražulis had publicly used derogatory terms to describe homosexual individuals and accused them of spreading sexually transmitted diseases. The court had concluded that his statements constituted mockery, humiliation, and incitement of hatred based on sexual orientation; however, the appellate court overturned the ruling, stating that mockery and humiliation as such do not amount to incitement of hatred. The case is now pending review by the Supreme Court of Lithuania. As Bikelis noted, Advertisement the appellate court ruling could reduce the likelihood of hate crime charges being brought in the Kaunas case, even though the incident involved a display of hostility toward Muslims that was particularly aggressive and intimidating. Bikelis criticized the slow response of Lithuanian politicians to the incident, pointing out that condemnation from the country's leaders could help prevent similar incidents from recurring. On the 14th of September, Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius called on all parties to refrain from escalating the situation. Parliamentary Speaker Juozas Olekas stated that differences of opinion regarding migration, religion, or other issues should not be expressed by humiliating others or interfering with religious rituals. Bikelis said he was particularly concerned by remarks from the Minister of National Defence, which implied that Muslims had somehow provoked the incident themselves. (Image: Police Scotland) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Police have launched an appeal to help trace a missing Edinburgh man who may have travelled to Glasgow before disappearing. Michal Oraczewski, 33, from the Wester Hailes area of Edinburgh, was last seen on Hailesland Grove on Monday, July 6. The 33-year-old was reported missing on September 3 and officers are now appealing for information on his whereabouts. Police said that during his last confirmed sighting, Michal indicated he was travelling to Glasgow for work. In the past, he has carried out contract cleaning work and officers are keen to hear from anyone who may have worked with him over the summer. Michal's first language is Polish, although he is said to speak fluent English. He is described as white, around 6ft tall and of slim build. When last seen, he was wearing dark blue jeans and a navy blue T-shirt. Inspector Paul Begley said: "Over the past two weeks we have conducted extensive enquiries in the Wester Hailes and surrounding areas in efforts to trace Michal. “I’m asking anyone who knows Michal, who may have seen him since July, or has any information on where he may be, to please get in touch. “I’d also like to directly appeal to Michal; if you see or hear about this appeal, please contact officers and let us know you are okay.” Anyone with information is being asked to contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting reference 1087 of September 3, 2026.
